reading.body:
Steve Stombres is named on 32 AI lobbying filings, and the clients behind them are ID.ME, LinkedIn, Instacart, Microsoft, the RIAA, and UKG.

The client list is the useful part. These are not model developers. They are identity verification, professional networking, grocery delivery, enterprise software, and music rights, which means the AI lobbying here is about how AI rules land on companies that deploy or are exposed to the technology rather than companies that build frontier models. The counts are uneven: ID.ME appears on 9 filings, LinkedIn and Instacart on 7 each, Microsoft on 5, the RIAA on 3, UKG on 1. All 32 filings route through a single lobbying firm.

The disclosed prior government positions are all congressional staff roles, ending with Chief of Staff in the Office of the Majority Leader from 2010 to 2014, with earlier stints for the Minority Whip, the Chief Deputy Majority Whip, and Congressman Eric Cantor. The Lobbying Disclosure Act requires filers to list covered positions held in the prior twenty years, so this is a disclosure requirement rather than a finding. One AI bill is named, S 2296, tied to a 2025 or later filing.

What this does not show is spending, outcomes, or what was said in any meeting. It records who was registered, for which clients, and which covered positions were reported. The data also notes that a different lobbyist shares the name, so the filings here belong to LDA lobbyist id 61629 and not to anyone else. Nothing here connects to data centers, power, or compute directly.

summary: Steve Stombres is named as a lobbyist on 32 Lobbying Disclosure Act filing(s) about AI held by this site. The firms, clients and AI bills on those filings are below. LDA lobbyist id 61629. A different lobbyist with the same name has a separate page.
